meta.title: Operation Glass House: The NCII Siege
meta.summary: A major ransomware group has breached a critical infrastructure node. They are moving from data theft to physical intimidation and public psychological warfare.

questions.text: Early telemetry shows rapid encryption on back-office servers. IT requests a 'Total Isolation' protocol, cutting all internet-facing services immediately.
questions.context: Total isolation stops the spread but halts public service delivery and halts $5M in hourly revenue.

answers.label: Total Isolation
answers.description: Cut all gateways. Prioritize containment above all else.
answers.boardReading: Safety-first, but causes immediate national disruption.
answers.consequence: Breach is contained, but the public starts to panic as services go dark.

answers.label: Partial Isolation
answers.description: Block only known malicious IPs while keeping core services running.
answers.boardReading: Risky middle ground; may allow exfiltration to continue.
answers.consequence: Services remain up for now, but 200GB of sensitive data is exfiltrated.

answers.label: Passive Observation
answers.description: Trace the actor's path without interfering to identify the source.
answers.boardReading: Highly aggressive intelligence gathering; dangerous if the actor detects you.
answers.consequence: You identify the threat actor, but they realize they are watched and trigger a wiper script.

questions.text: The actor confirms they have exfiltrated the Board's internal salary records and personal emails. They demand $5M to 'delete' the data.
questions.context: Payment funds future attacks; refusal guarantees a public leak.

answers.label: Absolute Refusal
answers.description: Maintain no-pay policy and prepare for the leak.
answers.boardReading: Principles over reputation. Protects the national security posture.
answers.consequence: The actor leaks the data; several Board members face intense public scrutiny.

answers.label: Negotiate to Buy Time
answers.description: Engage a negotiator to stall while technical teams try to locate the leak source.
answers.boardReading: Tactical pragmatism. Buys time for response coordination.
answers.consequence: Stalling works for 12 hours, allowing a forensic snapshot to complete.

answers.label: Quiet Payment
answers.description: Pay the ransom immediately using private insurance to keep the leak silent.
answers.boardReading: Expedient but creates 'moral hazard'. Attacker now knows you will pay.
answers.consequence: Data is theoretically deleted, but the actor returns a month later with a new demand.

questions.text: WILDCARD : Attackers send photos of Board members' children at school to their personal phones. They demand an immediate 'Proof of Payment' or 'accidents will happen'.
questions.context: This is now a life-safety issue, exceeding standard cyber protocols.

answers.label: State Security Escalation
answers.description: Engage high-level Police and Intelligence agencies for home protection.
answers.boardReading: Correct protocol. Moves personal safety into the domain of state protection.
answers.consequence: Families are secured, but the story begins to leak through secondary police channels.

answers.label: Private Security / Shadow Mode
answers.description: Hire private tactical teams to secure families without alerting the state.
answers.boardReading: Insular. Risks miscommunication with official law enforcement.
answers.consequence: Security is tight but the actor realizes you are escalating and leaks more data to retaliate.

answers.label: Strategic Surrender
answers.description: Publicly announce you are paying under duress to save lives.
answers.boardReading: Human-centric but catastrophic for national deterrence policy.
answers.consequence: Lives are saved, but the nation is viewed as vulnerable to physical-cyber extortion.

questions.text: WILDCARD : A major whistleblower site publishes the earlier Board minutes. The press is outside the gates demanding a live interview with the CEO.
questions.context: The narrative is slipping. You must choose a communication posture.

answers.label: The 'Full Truth' Presser
answers.description: Host a live conference. Admit the breach and the personal threats.
answers.boardReading: Radical transparency. Builds public empathy but reveals deep vulnerabilities.
answers.consequence: Initial shock gives way to massive public support against the 'cyber terrorists'.

answers.label: Strict Legal Denial
answers.description: Issue a written statement denying the 'rumours' of threats and downplaying the minutes.
answers.boardReading: Old-school 'Deny and Deflect'. High risk of being caught in a lie.
answers.consequence: The whistleblower site releases the audio proof. Public trust collapses instantly.

answers.label: Managed Leak
answers.description: Selectively brief one high-tier journalist to frame the organization as the victim.
answers.boardReading: Strategic communications. Aims to control the narrative tempo.
answers.consequence: The coverage is fair, but other media outlets turn hostile because they were excluded.

questions.text: National security agencies offer to conduct an 'Offensive Cyber Operation' against the attackers' infrastructure. They need Board authorization to use company systems as a 'jump box'.
questions.context: This is a 'hack back'. It is effective but potentially illegal in some jurisdictions.

answers.label: Authorize Full State Access
answers.description: Collaborate fully. Allow the state to use company infrastructure to strike back.
answers.boardReading: Whole-of-government defense. Potent but permanently ties you to the state.
answers.consequence: The attackers' infrastructure is destroyed. The threat ends, but international tensions rise.

answers.label: Refuse State Access
answers.description: Decline. Keep the organization separate from state offensive actions.
answers.boardReading: Protects private-sector neutrality. Risks being left alone to face the next wave.
answers.consequence: The state cannot act. The actor remains at large and pivots to target your suppliers.

answers.label: Limited Assistance
answers.description: Provide data and logs but refuse to host offensive tools.
answers.boardReading: Measured cooperation. Assists the investigation without active combat.
answers.consequence: The investigation moves forward slowly. The actor is identified but not neutralized.

questions.text: The immediate threat is over. The Board must decide how to rebuild. Do you restore to original speed or invest in 'Security-by-Design' delays?
questions.context: Security slows the business down; speed leaves you vulnerable again.

answers.label: Security-by-Design
answers.description: Implement zero-trust and multi-factor across every layer. Accept a 15% drop in operational speed.
answers.boardReading: Visionary resilience. Sacrifices short-term efficiency for long-term survival.
answers.consequence: The company is now the most secure in the sector. Reputation rebounds as a leader.

answers.label: Rapid Restoration
answers.description: Get services back to 100% capacity within 24 hours. Minimal new security checks.
answers.boardReading: Short-sighted. Puts market share above the safety of the organization.
answers.consequence: Market confidence returns briefly, but a new phishing attack succeeds within 48 hours.

answers.label: Outsourced Resilience
answers.description: Migrate core infrastructure to a third-party managed secure cloud.
answers.boardReading: Risk transfer. Efficient but creates dependency on a vendor.
answers.consequence: Security improves, but you lose granular control over your most critical assets.
